note: Source of truth for scripts/style_gate.py. Human-readable rationale and corpus evidence: gate_mechanical.md. Severities: FAIL = fix before the text ships; WARN = fix or justify in the audit ledger; INFO = report only. 'max_hits' is the number of hits tolerated per document before the rule fires.

rules.name: dash used as punctuation (---, em-dash, spaced --)
rules.fix: use a comma, parentheses, a colon or a new sentence (98% of corpus papers contain no dash)

rules.name: exclamation mark in prose
rules.fix: delete; state the fact

rules.name: conversational / hype word with zero corpus frequency
rules.fix: delete, or replace by the measured fact (a number in the results section, a contrast with prior work in the intro)

rules.name: hype word used in <=3% of corpus papers
rules.fix: delete, or state the measured fact

rules.name: contraction
rules.fix: write the full form (possessive 's is fine)

rules.name: 'Figure' spelled out before a reference (corpus: always 'Fig.')
rules.fix: write Fig.~\ref{...} (plural Figs.~\ref{..} and \ref{..})

rules.name: Eq./Equation before an equation reference (corpus: bare '(12)')
rules.fix: cite equations as \eqref{...} without the word 'Eq.'

rules.name: i.e. / e.g. not followed by a comma
rules.fix: write i.e., / e.g., (the comma is present in 99% of the corpus's uses; a few papers omit it)

rules.name: Firstly / Secondly / Thirdly / Lastly
rules.fix: 'First, / Second, / Finally,' is the majority style; Firstly/Lastly appear in ~20% of papers

rules.name: duplicated function word (the the, is is ...)
rules.fix: delete the repeat

rules.name: straight double quote in the source
rules.fix: use ``text'' in LaTeX

rules.name: sentence longer than 100 words
rules.fix: split; the corpus p95 for >60-word sentences is 0.7 per 1k words

rules.name: sentences longer than 60 words (rate cap)
rules.fix: split at the 'which' / 'where' / 'while' clause; cap = corpus p95 (0.8 per 1k words)

rules.name: sentences longer than 45 words (rate cap)
rules.fix: corpus: p50 1.0 / p90 2.6 per 1k words; mean sentence length is 24 words, p90 37

rules.name: section heading not in Title Case (89% of corpus papers use Title Case)
rules.fix: Title Case is the norm (89%); three 2025-26 papers use sentence case, so keep one style within a paper

rules.name: separate Related Work / Background section
rules.fix: 0/85 technical papers have one; the prior-art review sits in the Introduction

rules.name: abstract length / content
rules.fix: keep the abstract inside the register range (letter ~180 words, conference ~195, full ~268, tutorial ~190); no citations, no display math

rules.name: figure caption has more than one sentence
rules.fix: 96% of corpus captions are one sentence; move interpretation into the running text

rules.name: figure caption lacks final period
rules.fix: end figure captions with a period (94%)

rules.name: figure caption longer than 25 words
rules.fix: median is 8 words, p75 12; state the quantity versus the swept variable and the fixed parameters

rules.name: figure caption in Title Case
rules.fix: figure captions use sentence case (88%); acronyms and proper nouns may be capitalised

rules.name: \subfloat[] labels without (a), (b) in the caption
rules.fix: the group writes empty \subfloat[] and enumerates '(a) ...; (b) ...' inside the main caption

rules.name: table caption below the tabular
rules.fix: IEEE tables: caption above

rules.name: algorithm caption ends with a period
rules.fix: 87% of algorithm captions have no final period (Title Case, e.g. 'Proposed Algorithm for Solving (P1)')

rules.name: display equations without final , or .
rules.fix: equations are part of sentences: end with a comma when 'where ...' follows, a period otherwise

rules.name: contribution list form
rules.fix: 3 plain-sentence items of ~110 words; see rhetorical_moves.md

rules.name: agentless 'is proposed / was studied' in abstract or conclusion
rules.fix: both 'we propose ...' and 'is proposed' occur (45% of papers use the agentless form in the abstract or conclusion); recent papers prefer 'we'

rules.name: quality adjective used more than the corpus does
rules.fix: corpus: 'novel' in 21% of papers at 0.06 per 1k words; claim novelty by contrast ('Unlike existing works ...')

rules.name: weak qualifier
rules.fix: delete, or replace by the quantity

rules.name: leverage / utilize
rules.fix: use / employ / apply (corpus: ~1.5 per paper)

rules.name: wordy connective
rules.regex: \b(?:in order to|so as to|the fact that|owing to the fact|it is important to note|it should be noted that|it is interesting to note)\b
rules.fix: to / because / delete

rules.name: additive connectors stacked in one paragraph
rules.fix: at most three of Moreover / Furthermore / Additionally / In addition / Besides per paragraph

rules.name: three consecutive sentences start with 'We'
rules.fix: front-load a purpose or condition: 'To ..., we ...', 'Based on ..., we ...'

rules.name: etc. / and so on
rules.fix: close lists with 'among others' or name the last item

rules.name: priority claim
rules.fix: corpus: 'for the first time' in 1% of papers; contrast with named prior work instead

rules.name: sentence starting with And / But / So
rules.fix: However, / Moreover, / Hence,

rules.name: first person singular
rules.fix: the group writes 'we' even for single-author papers
